title: Progress ticks under bypass, and an evidence-based lane demotion checkpoint (spec #81 P4 + P3)
action: Spec #81, P4 then P3. (P4 TICKS) Under gate bypass the chat is silent between start and final report except the gate auto-approve lines, so perceived latency is the whole pipeline even when cells finish in minutes. Emit ONE line, never a question, at each of: cell cap, slice close, wave completion, a re-lane decision, and (when they exist) draft-PR creation and demo comments. Shape them like the examples in the spec: a check mark, the unit, and the outcome - cell id plus verify summary; slice number plus cell count plus test result. Add a config key `quiet` (boolean, default false) that suppresses the tick stream; `ship_visibility: off` also suppresses it. Ticks are agent chat output, so this is instruction text plus the config read - no new emitter machinery. (P3 RE-LANE) Lane is fixed at triage from the request text alone, uncertainty resolves upward, and nothing re-examines it once evidence exists, so an ambiguous request for a two-file change pays the full standard pipeline. Add ONE re-lane checkpoint immediately after the first evidence pass: exploring's scout for standard and above, or planning's orient when exploring was skipped. Demotion requires ALL THREE measured conditions: a counted product-file touch set within the target lane's threshold (small is three or fewer), zero hard-gate flags on that touch set, and no unresolved gray areas left in scope. Demotion is at most ONE step (standard to small; never into tiny, which stays triage-only), happens at most ONCE per feature, and is logged as a one-line audit decision naming the evidence counts. Promotion on discovered risk stays available at any time, unchanged. High-risk with any hard-gate flag can never demote regardless of file count. The triage guessing rule and its resolve-upward discipline are unchanged: this checkpoint converts measured evidence into a smaller lane, never optimism. (WEIGHT) These four skills total 96KB and spec #78 exists because they are already over-weight. Every line you add must replace one; put the re-lane mechanics in a reference and leave ONE routing line in bee-hive's body. Do not grow any body.

truths: The tick contract is stated once, names every event that emits one, and is honored from bee-swarming's orchestration text.
A `quiet` config key suppresses ticks, and so does ship_visibility off; the default is a live tick stream under bypass.
The re-lane checkpoint exists at exactly one place per path (exploring's scout, or planning's orient when exploring was skipped), fires at most once per feature, and demotes at most one step.
All three demotion conditions are required and are stated as measured, not argued; the hard-gate floor and the never-into-tiny rule are explicit.
A demotion logs a one-line audit decision naming the evidence counts.
Promotion on discovered risk is explicitly still available at any time.
No skill body grew: report the before and after byte count of every SKILL.md you touched.
prohibitions: Do NOT change gate semantics, bypass levels, proof-tier or evidence law.
Do NOT let the checkpoint re-argue flag counts - it uses the scouted touch set.
Do NOT allow a demotion into tiny, a second demotion, or any demotion of high-risk work carrying a hard-gate flag.
Do NOT grow any SKILL.md body; move text to references instead.

title: One review wave, one merged reviewer, one checker pass (spec #77 P2 + P3 + P4)
action: Spec #77, P2 P3 P4 together - they touch one dispatch path and the spec's own rollout order ships them as one batch. Today a standard slice pays a serial chain: orient worker, then plan-checker, then cell reviewer, each a separate dispatch over largely the same inputs, with the checker looping up to three iterations. (P2 ONE WAVE) Dispatch simultaneously at stage start: the merged reviewer, and the orient/extraction worker when the delegation rubric fires. The orchestrator runs the reality gate and feasibility matrix on the session model WHILE the wave runs. Sync point unchanged: Gate 3 presentation, or its bypass self-approval, still cannot happen while any wave member is outstanding. (P3 MERGED REVIEWER) One bee-review-class dispatch with a two-part mandate: the adversarial structural check over its existing five dimensions, and the cold-pickup cell review with its existing flags. Findings keep BOTH existing vocabularies - BLOCKER and WARNING for structure, CRITICAL and MINOR for cells - in two sections of one report. High-risk persona-panel scaling applies to this merged dispatch unchanged. Same review slot, same tier resolution, same read-only gather contract. (P4 ONE-SHOT CHECKER) The merged reviewer runs ONCE. WARNING-level and mechanically fixable findings (a missing link, a vague verify command, a dependency typo) are applied directly by the orchestrator to the cells, which is legal because cells are mutable before Gate 3. Only unresolved BLOCKERs trigger a second and final pass scoped to those blockers. There is no third iteration; open BLOCKERs after pass two escalate to the user exactly as iteration-three escalation does today. (WEIGHT) bee-validating is 17KB and spec #78 exists because these skills are over-weight: every line you add must replace one, and the merged reviewer's prompt belongs in the reference, not the body. Note fs-2 already added the delta-validation rule to this skill - read it first so the wave and the delta rule compose rather than contradict.

truths: The reviewer and the orient worker are dispatched together at stage start, and the orchestrator's own matrix work is stated as running concurrently with them.
Gate 3 still cannot be presented or self-approved while any wave member is outstanding.
One reviewer dispatch replaces two, carrying both mandates and both finding vocabularies in one report with two sections.
The checker runs once; WARNING-level and mechanically fixable findings are orchestrator-applied to the cells; only unresolved BLOCKERs get a second and final pass.
There is never a third iteration, and the existing escalation path is unchanged.
The merged reviewer prompt lives in the reference, not the body; report bee-validating's before and after byte count.
The new wave text composes with fs-2's delta-validation rule rather than contradicting it.
prohibitions: Do NOT change Gate 3 semantics, the advisor consult enforcement, or spike discipline - spec #77 P5 was rejected, so runtime spikes stay mandatory on standard lane.
Do NOT drop a finding class when merging the two reviewers; both vocabularies survive.
Do NOT allow a third verification iteration.
Do NOT grow the bee-validating body.
